keyRules: Maximum flight altitude is 120 m (400 ft) above ground level.

Drones ('Small') up to 25 kg used exclusively for recreation do not require registration, an airworthiness certificate or an operator permit from DINACIA — but they may not fly above 120 m, nor fly in controlled airspace or an aerodrome traffic zone without ATM authorization.

In Montevideo, DINACIA has designated 4 recreational flying zones for Small drones (up to 25 kg), in defined sectors of: Parque Baroffio (northern area), Parque Marcos Sastre (near Ruta 8), Parque Miguelete (stretch between Silva and Bvar. Aparicio Saravia) and Parque Tomkinson (except the baby football club area). Maximum altitude in these zones: 30 m above ground (DINACIA Res. 093/2019, AIP ENR 5.5).
Drones from 25 to 260 kg ('Medium') must be registered with DINACIA and receive an identification number visible on the device.
The pilot must keep the drone within direct line of sight at all times.
Flying over densely populated areas (cities, towns, neighborhoods) is not permitted without express authorization from the aeronautical authority.
Avoid airports, airfields, and controlled airspace (CTR) unless expressly authorized.
A reasonable distance from people and buildings not involved (recommended: 30 m)
Always fly in visual meteorological conditions (VMC); flying only during daytime is recommended.
Commercial use requires mandatory civil liability or aviation insurance, in addition to the corresponding DINACIA permit.

Operations requiring express authorization (over populated areas or gatherings of people, in aerodrome zones, in prohibited or restricted areas, or for commercial use): apply to DINACIA via the UTM platform (utm.dinacia.gub.uy).
importantNotes: Uruguay is relatively permissive: DINACIA Resolution 291/2014 states that drones up to 25 kg do not require registration for recreational use.
DINACIA Resolution 291/2014 classifies drones into three categories: Small (≤25 kg), Medium (25-260 kg) and Large (over 260 kg).

The rules also apply to non-residents. For exclusively recreational use of a drone up to 25 kg, no registration or operator permit is required. All paid use (even with small drones) requires the DINACIA DAOD Operator Permit (requirements: 18 years of age, a course at an authorized center, a skills test and Uruguayan citizenship; foreigners must open an APIA electronic file with DINACIA) and civil liability insurance.

🚫 PROHIBITED ZONES (AIP ENR 5.1): Torre Ejecutiva/Plaza Independencia in Montevideo (950 m radius), Residencia Presidencial Suárez (950 m radius), Estancia Presidencial Anchorena (1,852 m radius), Isla de Lobos off Punta del Este (5 km radius), islands off Cabo Polonio, Barra de Valizas and La Coronilla (5 km radius), military units, prisons, dams and ANCAP fuel plants. ATM authorization is required in the controlled airspace and traffic zone of Carrasco (MVD) and Laguna del Sauce (PDP) airports. Coasts and beaches are often densely populated in high season.

🌳 PROTECTED NATURAL AREAS (SNAP): The National System of Protected Areas includes areas such as Esteros de Farrapos, Cabo Polonio, and Quebrada de los Cuervos. Check with the Ministry of the Environment for specific restrictions before operating drones in these areas.

fields.disclaimerText: Always check DINACIA’s official sources before flying. This app is a tool, not a legal authority. Uruguay enforces DINACIA Resolution 291/2014 and the Uruguayan Aeronautical Regulations (RAU). Drones up to 25 kg used exclusively for recreation do not require registration; those used commercially and those over 25 kg do.
